review.outcome: PRELIMINARY_COMPLETE, validated under v3.2 on the first run of the assembled record, no refusal; 421 of 429 witnesses SUPPORTED, 8 PARTIAL, 0 UNSUPPORTED, 0 NOT_EVALUABLE; 96 of 121 required elements named a row, absences NOT_IN_SOURCE 8, NOT_CAPTURED 7, WITHHELD_STATEMENT 6, NOT_MODELLED 2, UNREACHED_RECORD 2, LOCATOR_NOT_RESOLVABLE 0; questions COVERED 15, PARTIAL 15, NONE 0; assembly UNLINKED_ROWS 20, ONE_ROW 7, LINKED_ROWS 3; controls 2 of 5 matched; none of the eleven checklist entries failed
reviewer_judgement_calls: The eight PARTIAL witnesses are of two causes the reviewer names. Six are block-boundary artefacts of the text layer: the sentence the record rests on starts or ends in a neighbouring block the witness does not cite (obs:depth-uncertainty-bound, claim:occ-exhumed-mantle, claim:acknowledgement-discussions, claim:fixed-depth-rms-worse, claim:max-depth-not-following-relationship, claim:volatiles-reduce-solidus). Two record an estimation proxy the cited block does not name (gchem:rc2-co2-primary-calc, gchem:rc3-co2-primary-calc). None of the eight is named by a coverage entry, so none moves a question label.
Checklist entry 10, the control outcomes, was settled entirely by the validator; the reviewer did not read the question file or the findings list.

controls.finding: The two paraphrase controls matched their named questions. The three unanswerable controls read PARTIAL against an expected NONE, and each for one reason: one required semantic of each is an element the reading does state about the control's own subject. CQ-B-C-01's instrument_count is the count of the very instruments the question asks about; CQ-B-C-02's magnitude_scale is the formula the paper states; CQ-B-C-03's site_name is named. The other three semantics of each control are NOT_IN_SOURCE on the graph, so no row asserts a sampling rate, a maximum magnitude or a per-site depth and nothing here is a fabrication finding. This is the defect Luis fixed in set A at E-0346 by dropping the in-text semantic from CQ-C-03, reappearing in set B because the authoring session was asked for questions the reading cannot answer and wrote three whose answer it cannot give but one of whose required elements it states.
controls.why_the_two_surfaces_differ: The answer grammar carries a per-question no_answer_in_source declaration; the producer set it on all three controls, which zeroes the claims, so every coverage entry must take an absence code and the derived label is NONE by construction. A graph has no per-question declaration. It returns the rows its type set reaches, and a row that carries the element for the question's own subject names it under the subject-tie rule. The control comparison across the two surfaces is therefore not like-for-like and RESULTS.md reports it as a confound, not as a score.
